Definition: from a variation of G1373; to thirst for (literally or figuratively):--(be, be a-)thirst(-y).
BiblicalUsage: To thirst, the ache Jesus blesses in those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, and the thirst He promises to satisfy forever. The woman at the well heard that whoever drinks the water He gives will never thirst again, and the Spirit and the bride still call the thirsty to come and drink freely.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe thirst is the honest shape of faith: I come empty and He fills me. The water Jesus gives is not a ration but a spring, and the invitation at the end of the Bible is still open to anyone who thirsts.
